candidate_relations.label: Myocardial Infarction, acute
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents an acute MI (ST elevation in inferior-posterior leads, elevated cTnT and CK-MB, occlusive LCx thrombus), but the benchmark reference specifies the complication of LV free wall rupture following AMI. The CTA showing contrast leakage from myocardium to pericardial cavity and echocardiography showing circumferential pericardial effusion confirm free wall rupture. Acute MI alone is the parent/cause but omits the critical mechanical complication that defines the final diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Acute MI is the underlying cause/parent condition; the reference diagnosis requires the specific mechanical complication of left ventricular free wall rupture as the final diagnostic object

case_quality_flags: CTA contrast leakage from myocardium to pericardial cavity is pathognomonic for LV free wall rupture; this key finding distinguishes the final diagnosis from uncomplicated AMI
Hemodynamic instability and post-procedural deterioration with back pain and hypoxia are consistent with cardiac tamponade secondary to free wall rupture
